output.summary: A tree endemic to eastern Australia, the silk oak has deeply divided leaves and golden-yellow to orange flowers with red blotches. Indigenous Australians traditionally consumed its rich nectar directly from the blossom or shaken into water, although the flowers and fruit contain toxic hydrogen cyanide.
